canada.title: Majority of Nova Scotians have opted in to race-based health data project — what will it tell us?
canada.summary: Nearly 695,000 Nova Scotians have now shared their race and linguistic identities with the province’s Health Department, creating a dataset that will eventually be used to analyze — and ideally correct — inequities in the health-care system.

canada.title: Physician Assistants are new to Nova Scotia, but the health authority says they're already cutting wait times
canada.summary: Nova Scotia Health plans to expand the use of a little-known role in the health care system that it says is helping cut wait times.

canada.title: Reliance on private nurses draining Interlake First Nation's personal care home budget
canada.summary: A Manitoba First Nation facing a shortage of health-care workers is relying on nurses from private agencies to help staff its personal care home, draining the facility's budget and forcing its overburdened personnel to handle tasks the outside nurses won't handle.

canada.title: Manitoba Hydro says provincial economy, electrification could slow with only 1 new gas turbine in Brandon
canada.summary: Manitoba Hydro says economic growth and the green-energy transition in this province could slow down if the NDP government follows through on a recommendation to downsize the planned expansion of the Brandon generating station.

canada.title: Sudbury police raise questions over closure of Cecil Facer Youth Centre
canada.summary: The decades-old boy's detention centre in Greater Sudbury will close at the end of November, but Greater Sudbury Police and Sudbury NDP MPP Jamie West say they still don't know the province's official rationale for shuttering Cecil Facer.

canada.title: Dieppe school debate turns on different views of equality
canada.summary: In legal terms, anglophones in Dieppe and Memramcook have a right to a school in their language because they have the numbers. But francophones opposed to the anglophone school proposed for Dieppe frame the issue in a different way.

canada.title: Fredericton hospital ER facing capacity 'crisis' that needs urgent fix, says doctor
canada.summary: Demands on staff and resources at the Dr. Everett Chalmers Regional Hospital is at a crisis point, largely due to an inability to promptly move discharged patients into long-term care facilities, said Dr. Yogi Sehgal.

canada.title: Amid cuts, expensive contracts at MUN, ‘we all need to worry’: faculty association
canada.summary: MUN's faculty association president Erika Merschrod says how the university is spending public money, including on expensive firms, is “a huge concern.” It comes as MUN cuts positions, courses and looks to sell properties. Unions representing students are also worried about the quality education they are being offered.

canada.title: 'They definitely heard our voices:' N.L. cadets relieved after government tops up program funding
canada.summary: N.L. cadets and alumni are rejoicing after the Defence Department made the decision on Monday to top up funding allowing cadet training activities to continue.

canada.title: Danielle Smith’s hold over UCP takes centre stage as 7,000 members registered for annual meeting
canada.summary: Alberta's United Conservatives kick off their fifth annual general meeting under Premier Danielle Smith Friday, a gathering expected to reveal much about the party’s future a little more than a month after a divisive referendum.

canada.title: Quebec government's appeal of oath to King ruling to be heard today
canada.summary: Earlier this week, a judge ruled that members of Quebec's provincial legislature must swear allegiance to the Crown before sitting at the National Assembly. He warned that any laws passed could be rendered invalid if members do not take the oath.

canada.title: Ford, Unifor call on Ottawa to exempt Canadian automakers from exhaust pollution penalties
canada.summary: Ontario Premier Doug Ford and Unifor president Lana Payne are calling on Ottawa to exempt automakers from penalties for failing to comply with the government's tailpipe emission standards.

canada.title: Trina Hunt’s family alleges husband killed her, seeks return of assets in B.C. lawsuit
canada.summary: A new civil claim alleges Iain Hunt killed his wife and should be barred from benefiting financially from her death. The allegations have not been proven in court.

canada.title: Yukon power infrastructure project now at Carney's Major Projects Office
canada.summary: On Thursday evening, Prime Minister Mark Carney announced he would be referring the Whitehorse Power Centres project to the Major Projects Office. The project, which will see a federal investment of up to $73 million, includes two new thermal power plants, a new electrical substation and transmission infrastructure in Whitehorse.
